title: How to choose a Kundan necklace for your lehenga neckline
description: Match your Kundan necklace to your blouse neckline: what works for sweetheart, deep V, round, boat, high-neck and off-shoulder lehenga blouses.
intro: Start with the blouse, not the necklace. A Kundan set that looks stunning in its box can crowd a high neck or float lost inside a deep V. The simplest rule: let the shape of your neckline decide the shape and length of the necklace, then let the lehenga's colours decide the stones.

sections.heading: Why the neckline matters more than the set
paragraphs: The bare skin between your chin and the edge of your blouse works like a frame. A necklace should sit inside that frame with a little breathing room, roughly one or two finger-widths above the fabric. When the necklace touches or overlaps the neckline, the two compete and both look busier in photos.

Kundan is flat and broad by nature. The stones are set close together on a base, so even a medium piece covers a lot of skin. That is why Kundan needs more open space than a delicate chain does, and why getting the neckline match right is half the job.

sections.heading: Sweetheart and U-shaped necklines
paragraphs: These are the easiest blouses to style. The curve of the neckline already looks like a necklace, so a rounded Kundan piece that follows the same curve looks natural. A choker paired with a slightly longer rani haar works very well here because both layers echo the U shape.
Keep the lowest point of your necklace a little above the dip of the sweetheart. If the pendant drops into the neckline, it gets hidden by the fabric edge, and the effect is lost.

sections.heading: Deep V necklines
paragraphs: A deep V leaves a long, narrow triangle of skin. A short round choker on its own leaves the lower part of that triangle empty, which can look unfinished. Go for a necklace with a pointed or drop-shaped centre, or a long haar whose pendant lands just above where the V closes.
If you love chokers, layer one with a longer piece so the eye travels down the V. Two layers are usually enough. Three can work on a very deep V, but only if the blouse itself is simple.

sections.heading: Round, boat and square necks
paragraphs: A round neck that sits close to the collarbone suits a short necklace or collar-style choker that sits neatly above it. Avoid long pieces that hang over the blouse and bounce on the embroidery.
Boat necks are wide and horizontal, so they leave a broad band of skin across the collarbones. A wide choker or bib-style Kundan necklace fills that space beautifully. A thin chain looks lost here.

Square necklines pair well with necklaces that have some angle to them, such as a squared-off pendant or a layered set where each layer sits in a straight line. A heavily rounded piece is not wrong, but it softens the sharp shape you chose the blouse for.

sections.heading: High necks, collars and off-shoulder blouses
paragraphs: High-neck and collared blouses leave almost no space at the throat. You have two good options. Skip the necklace and put the attention on statement earrings, a maang tikka or a passa. Or wear one long haar over the blouse so it rests on the fabric below the collar. A choker squeezed above a high neck rarely sits comfortably.
Off-shoulder and very wide necklines show the most skin, so they can carry the most jewellery. A broad choker, a bib necklace or a choker and haar combination all look balanced here.

sections.heading: Matching the Kundan to the lehenga itself
paragraphs: Once the shape is settled, look at colour. Pick one stone or bead colour that already appears in your embroidery, such as the green in the border or the pink in the motifs, rather than trying to match everything. Gold zari work sits naturally with gold-plated Kundan. If your lehenga has a lot of silver or tilla work, consider whether a gold-toned set will clash, or bring in a set with more white stones to bridge the two.

Heavy embroidery on the blouse means a cleaner necklace. A plain or lightly worked blouse can take a richer set. Also think about the dupatta: if it is pinned over one shoulder, it will cover part of a wide necklace, so check the drape before you decide. You can browse shapes and lengths among our [Kundan necklace sets](/women/necklaces) to compare.

sections.heading: A quick trial before the wedding day
paragraphs: Do a proper trial at least a week ahead, with the actual blouse and dupatta, not a similar top.
list: Wear the blouse and necklace together and take a phone photo from about six feet away, the way a photographer would.
Check that the necklace does not touch or overlap the blouse edge.
Pin the dupatta the way you plan to and see what it hides.
Wear the set for twenty minutes to judge weight and whether the back hook or dori sits comfortably.
Add the earrings and tikka so you see the full balance, not just the necklace alone.

faq.q: Can I wear a Kundan choker with a high-neck blouse?
faq.a: It is usually uncomfortable and looks crowded. A long haar worn over the blouse, or skipping the necklace for bold earrings, tends to look better.

faq.q: Should the Kundan stones match my lehenga exactly?
faq.a: No. Pick one colour that already appears in the embroidery. An exact match everywhere can look flat.

faq.q: How long should a necklace be for a deep V neck?
faq.a: Aim for the pendant or lowest point to sit just above where the V closes, so it stays visible and is not hidden by fabric.

faq.q: Does gold-plated Kundan work with a silver-toned lehenga?
faq.a: It can, but check in daylight. Sets with more white stones usually bridge gold jewellery and silver embroidery more smoothly.
